text.p: Motorola Inc said Monday it terminated 170 employees at its semiconductor sector in Austin, Tex., in a continuing effort to cut spending.
"They are a reduction in work force," said Dan Rogers, director of public affairs for the company's semiconductor sector. "We're continuing cost cutting."
The jobs were cut from all categories of work, Rogers said, including manufacturing, non-manufacturing, professional and technician.

Earlier this month, Motorola offered some 6,000 mnaufacturing employees in the semiconductor sector voluntary severance packages. That offer was an extension of one made to non-manufacturing workers in the group in July.
Rogers declined to say if the company did not get the necessary results from the offers.
"These were involuntary," Rogers said of Monday's job cuts.

Earlier this month, Motorola reported a 58 percent drop in third quarter earnings compared with last year, and said its semiconductor business, plagued with industry-wide overcapacity, essentially broke even.
The company said it would take fourth quarter charges of "several tens of millions of dollars" for cost-cutting measures, including reductions in work force.
In July, Motorola terminated 145 employees, also at its Austin facility, which were the company's first involuntary layoffs in more than a decade.
